title: Resource Drift, Refresh-Only, moved and removed Blocks

header.html: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state

Removing from state without destroying: the removed block

html:
1What drift is

Drift is a difference between the real infrastructure and what Terraform's state and configuration say. It happens when someone changes a resource outside Terraform (a console edit, another tool, an automatic process).

Situation What terraform plan does
A setting was changed outside Terraform Refreshes the state, sees the difference and proposes to change it back to match the configuration
A resource was deleted outside Terraform Proposes to create it again
A new resource appeared outside Terraform Ignores it: Terraform only manages what it created or imported
Exam tip

. Drift is found during plan (and apply) because Terraform refreshes the state first. The default fix is to apply the configuration, which overwrites the outside change.

2Refresh-only mode

You may want to accept the real values into the state without changing the infrastructure. Use refresh-only mode.

Command Effect
terraform plan -refresh-only Shows how the state would change to match reality; no infrastructure change
terraform apply -refresh-only Updates the state (after approval) to match reality
terraform refresh Older shortcut for the same, deprecated because it does not ask for approval

After a refresh-only apply, update the configuration if you also want the new values to be the desired state; otherwise the next normal plan will change them back.

Exam tip

. -refresh-only updates only the state. It never changes real infrastructure. terraform refresh is deprecated in favor of apply -refresh-only.

3Refactoring without destroying: the moved block

When you rename a resource or move it into a module, Terraform would normally destroy the old address and create the new one. A moved block tells Terraform that the object is the same and updates the state address instead.

moved {
  from = aws_instance.web
  to   = aws_instance.application
}
Fact Detail
Purpose Rename or relocate a resource or module without recreating it
Keep it? Keep it long enough for everyone to apply, then it may be removed
Alternative terraform state mv (a manual, one-time CLI change)

4Removing from state without destroying: the removed block

A removed block stops managing a resource without destroying the real object.

removed {
  from = aws_instance.old

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
Setting Effect
destroy = false Remove from state, keep the real object
destroy = true (the default if the block is just deleted) The object is destroyed

The CLI alternative is terraform state rm ADDRESS.

Exam tip

. moved renames without recreating. removed with destroy = false forgets without destroying. Deleting a resource block normally destroys the real object.

5Other state tools in this objective

Tool Use
terraform apply -replace=ADDRESS Recreate a resource that is broken
terraform state mv / rm Manual address changes and removal
Drift detection in HCP Terraform Scheduled health assessments that report drift (Module 16)

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Someone changed an instance's tags in the console. What does the next terraform plan show?

  • ANo change, because the console is not tracked
  • BAn error stating that the state is invalid
  • CA change to update the tags back to the configuration
  • DA change that deletes the state file
Show the answer

Answer: C. Plan refreshes the state, finds the difference and proposes to restore the configured values.

S2A team wants to accept the real values into the state without touching any infrastructure. What should they run?

  • Aterraform destroy -refresh-only
  • Bterraform apply -refresh-only
  • Cterraform init -refresh
  • Dterraform fmt -refresh
Show the answer

Answer: B. Refresh-only apply updates the state to match reality and changes no infrastructure.

S3A resource block is renamed from web to application. How can Terraform avoid destroying and recreating it?

  • AAdd a moved block with from and to
  • BAdd a lifecycle block with prevent_destroy
  • CAdd a data block for the old name
  • DRun terraform fmt on the file
Show the answer

Answer: A. A moved block tells Terraform the object is the same and updates its address in the state.

S4A team wants Terraform to stop managing a resource but leave the real object running. What should they use?

  • ADeleting the resource block only
  • BA removed block with destroy set to false
  • CA lifecycle block with ignore_changes set to all
  • DA depends_on block on the resource
Show the answer

Answer: B. A removed block with destroy = false removes the object from state and keeps the real resource.

S5Which command is deprecated because it updates state without asking for approval?

  • Aterraform plan
  • Bterraform validate
  • Cterraform show
  • Dterraform refresh
Show the answer

Answer: D. terraform refresh is deprecated; use apply with the refresh-only option.

S6A new resource was created manually outside Terraform and is not in the configuration. What does plan do?

  • AIt ignores the resource
  • BIt deletes the resource
  • CIt imports the resource automatically
  • DIt reports an error
Show the answer

Answer: A. Terraform manages only what it created or imported, so it ignores unmanaged objects.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is drift?

Show the answer

Real infrastructure differing from the state and configuration.

R2When does Terraform detect drift?

Show the answer

During plan and apply, when it refreshes the state.

R3What does refresh-only change?

Show the answer

Only the state.

R4What does a moved block do?

Show the answer

Renames or relocates an object without recreating it.

R5What does destroy = false in a removed block do?

Show the answer

Removes from state and keeps the real object.

R6What is the CLI command to remove from state?

Show the answer

terraform state rm.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Drift outside changes; found by plan; apply restores the configuration
Refresh-only plan or apply -refresh-only updates state only; terraform refresh deprecated
moved rename or move without recreating
removed destroy = false forgets without destroying; state rm is the CLI way
